title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.12942v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. We separate three questions: whether a model ranks churners well, whether that ranking earns more expected maximum profit (EMP), and whether its probabilities can drive a threshold policy. With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately. translated_title: 表格基础模型与调优梯度提升树在电信客户流失预测中的对比：基于利润与校准感知的评估
translated_abstract: 表格基础模型（TFM）能够在单次前向传播中基于有标注的上下文完成预测。近期一项基准测试报告称，在客户流失预测任务上，表格基础模型决定性地优于树集成模型，但该测试仅将其与未调优的梯度提升树（GBDT）进行比较，且只采用排序类指标评分，而留存营销活动的实际评判标准是金钱收益。我们在五个公开的电信客户流失数据集上、通过10个随机种子划分，将TabPFN-2.5、TabPFN-3.5、TabPFN-3.5-Fast和TabICL v2与经Optuna调优的GBDT进行了重新评估。我们区分了三个问题：模型是否能很好地对流失客户进行排序、该排序是否能带来更高的期望最大利润（EMP）、以及其概率输出能否支撑阈值策略。通过划分感知的检验方法并对20项预先声明的比较进行Holm校正，TabPFN-3.5在Cell2Cell（1.9%）和Iranian（7.6%）数据集上获得的EMP显著高于最优的调优GBDT，且这两项优势在与三个调优GBDT分别单独比较时依然成立。在Orange i……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究以期望最大利润和概率校准为评判标准，将表格基础模型与经Optuna调优的梯度提升树在电信客户流失预测上进行严格重新评估，发现TabPFN-3.5在部分数据集上能显著带来更高利润，修正了以往仅用排序指标、与未调优基线比较所得出的结论。
en_tdlr: This study re-evaluates tabular foundation models against Optuna-tuned gradient-boosted trees for telecom churn using profit- and calibration-aware metrics, showing that TabPFN-3.5 achieves significantly higher expected maximum profit on some datasets, thereby revising earlier conclusions based on untuned baselines and ranking-only metrics.
